item.title: AI adoption could put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk: JP Morgan
item.description: AI could put 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk globally over five years, according to JP Morgan, as businesses accelerate automation and AI adoption.
item.dc:creator: Sarjna Rai
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence (AI) could put around 24 million knowledge-worker jobs at risk worldwide over the next five years, as businesses increasingly use the technology to automate tasks currently performed by employees, according to a report by JP Morgan Wealth Management. The estimate is based on an illustrative scenario in which companies use AI to replace a portion of their workforce rather than simply improve productivity. However, the report cautions that the impact may be felt more through reduced hiring and unfilled vacancies than through large-scale layoffs. AI and employment According to the report, the potential displacement represents around 1.3 per cent of the global knowledge workforce every year over five years. This estimate assumes that half of enterprise spending on AI goes towards replacing jobs that would otherwise have been filled, while AI costs approximately half as much as the workers it replaces. The impact could be particularly significant if job losses are concentrated in specific occupations or regions, as this could create wider economic and political pressures. The analysis also highlighted the potential scale of disruption in the United States. If two-thirds of the displaced jobs were located there, around 16 million workers could be affected over five years, equivalent to approximately three million annually. This would represent around 2 per cent of US payrolls each year, more than four times the pace of manufacturing job losses during the 2000s. How AI may reshape work Despite the potential scale of displacement, the report said the more likely outcome would be a transformation of existing jobs rather than their complete elimination. The report noted that every job involves a collection of tasks, and AI currently can automate or support only some of them. This means employees may increasingly work alongside AI tools rather than be replaced entirely. It also pointed out that AI adoption across industries is likely to remain gradual and uneven, limiting the possibility of widespread job displacement in the immediate future. AI adoption still low The report highlighted that AI is still at an early stage of adoption, particularly outside the technology sector. In the United States, around 6 per cent of work hours are currently AI-assisted, even though nearly two-thirds of tasks could theoretically be exposed to the technology. For businesses to realise returns on their AI investments, adoption will need to extend beyond pilot projects and become more widespread across their operations. AI use expands in India The potential impact of AI on employment is also becoming increasingly relevant in India, where businesses are preparing to expand their use of the technology. According to a joint report by KPMG India and the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), 93 per cent of Indian business leaders plan to deploy AI agents to expand workforce capabilities, while 59 per cent are already using them to automate workstreams or business processes. The report also found that 74 per cent of Indian CEOs believe workforce readiness for AI will significantly influence business growth over the next three years. As AI takes over routine activities such as information retrieval, preparing first drafts and routine analysis, employees are expected to focus more on decision-making, interpreting information and evaluating AI-generated outputs.

item.content:encoded: Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates, Friday, Nov 27 2026: Tbenchmark indices declined as global technology shares extended recovery after weeks of volatility and as oil prices rose amid heightened volatility in West Asia.  As of 10:00 AM, the Sensex fell 261.76 points or 0.31 per cent to 84,066.83 and the Nifty50 was down 39.70 points or 0.15 per cent at 25,844.80. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCL Technologies, and Infosys were the top losers in the Nifty50.  In the broader markets, the Nifty MidCap 100 and the Nifty SmallCap 100 rose 0.43 per cent and 0.30 per cent, respectively. Sector-wise, Nifty IT declined the most, while Nifty Metal rose the most.  IPO TodayThe initial public offer (IPO) of Airpro Technology India will open for subscription on Friday. Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) IPO will enter the second day of subscription on Friday. The company is seeking to raise ₹360.76 crore. Shree Siddhivinayak Greentech Industries IPO will open for subscription on the final day. It’s a book-build issue worth ₹93.66 crore.

RBI's first state debt switch success opens door for more auctions: Traders The strong response has market participants anticipating more rounds of such switch auctions

A switch auction allows the issuer to buy back shorter-term bonds with near-term maturities, while selling longer-dated papers at the same time (Photo: Reuters)

Reuters MUMBAI 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 8:17 AM IST

Listen to This Article

The Reserve Bank of India's first ever switch of state government securities saw strong participation from lenders, leading to near full subscription.   The strong response has market participants anticipating more rounds of such switch auctions.   Indian states sold debt worth around ₹8,000 crore ($864.63 million) and bought back securities worth nearly ₹8,300 crore, the Reserve Bank of India said   A switch auction allows the issuer to buy back shorter-term bonds with near-term maturities, while selling longer-dated papers at the same time.   While the Indian federal government holds switch auctions at least once a month, such auctions for state government securities have not taken place before.

Bonds issued by the states of Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh were swapped at Thursday's auction.   "Some banks wanted to let go of the papers that are out of (the) money," a trader with a private bank said, replacing them with fresh notes that are easier to buy and sell.   "We could see more such auctions in the remaining part of the financial year," the trader added.   Indian states plan to borrow ₹2.78 trillion through bonds in the October-December quarter of the current fiscal year.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Saudi airstrikes hit Yemen, kill four as Houthi attacks target oil sites

Saudi airstrikes hit Yemen, kill four as Houthi attacks target oil sites Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry, said multiple strikes across Taiz province killed four people, including a child. Al-Asbahi blamed Saudi Arabia for the attacks

Smoke billows behind rubble at the site of a reported airstrike on warehouses north of Sanaa, Yemen | Image: Reuters

AP Dubai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 7:53 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Saudi airstrikes hit western and southwestern Yemen overnight and on Thursday, Houthi officials and media said. The group blamed the Saudi-backed government forces battling the rebels for the attacks. Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry, said multiple strikes across Taiz province killed four people, including a child. Al-Asbahi blamed Saudi Arabia for the attacks. Al-Masirah, the television channel controlled by the Iran-backed rebels, reported strikes in Sanaa overnight into Thursday. Two residents said they heard explosions in the rebel-held capital overnight. Khalil al-Makhlafi, who lives in the southern part of Sanaa, said his home is located near military camps in an area where explosions are frequent.

"We have to endure these sounds every now and then, and they have health implications for our kids," al-Makhlafi said. The second resident, Randa al-Mahwiti, reported hearing explosions in the northern part of Sanaa. The latest attacks come as part of the ongoing renewed fighting between the rebels and the Saudi-backed government forces. The Associated Press couldn't independently verify the claims made by Al-Asbahi, the rebel spokesman, or Al-Masirah, the rebel-run television channel. Also on Thursday, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said an attack on an oil refinery in the kingdom's southwest killed a Nepalese worker. Since their fighting with the kingdom escalated over the summer, the Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi oil facilities, including the Jazan refinery that was attacked again on Thursday.
